SHAPE OF THE DAY, stated first because it is the finding rather than a shortfall: this is a DE-RISKING report. Seven of the fourteen rows are position closes, five are holds with levels essentially unchanged, one is continuing long-term accumulation, and exactly ONE is a new directional entry (GDX short) — the first in four runs. The reason is a sourced regime change, not caution: the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 for the first time since 2023, 16 of 18 dots see another this year, the 10-year is at a 19-year high of 5.27%, and Monday's 3-4% gold and silver break was that impulse reading through the asset it hurts most. This book was built full of long-duration equity theses and a hiking cycle de-rates exactly those.

SEVEN CLOSES NEED AN ORDER AT TODAY'S OPEN, and they are named here in plain words because the enforcement pass will demote every one of them to the watchlist for having no entry and no target — which is what a close is. SELL to close: CEG, CCJ, NKE, SNX, LULU, LCII. BUY to close: the TLT short (a take-profit at +3.97%). If a demoted row is the only place a reader looks, the instruction is still here.

THE RULE APPLIED TO THOSE SEVEN WAS STRUCTURE, NOT P&L, and it is checkable. Every position closed had either NO STOP with a target 15-27 ATR away (NKE, LULU, LCII), or a stop inside 1.5 ATR with an unreachable target (CEG at 1.19 ATR against a 6.8 ATR target, CCJ at 1.46 against 15.4), or a stop below the publishable floor that breaks the ratio when widened to it (SNX: 1.40 ATR against a 2.0 floor, and at a compliant 234.92 stop the ratio falls to 1.45). Meanwhile losing positions with sound structure were HELD — XLE -2.9%, DINO -1.2%, SVRA -5.2% — and the single best winner in the book was CLOSED, TLT at +3.97%, because 0.74 ATR of remaining reward against 5.56 ATR of give-back is not a position worth carrying through PCE. A rule that closes a winner and holds losers is not a rule about the mark.

ONE LEVEL WAS AMENDED IN SYNTHESIS, in the direction that makes the trade worse: DINO's stop moves DOWN from 97.75 to 97.28. The research phase flagged 97.75 as 1.91 ATR from the 107.50 entry against a 2.0 stock floor rather than hiding it; 97.28 is exactly 2.00 ATR on the re-fetched ATR14 of 5.1087, and with the 128.00 target untouched the recomputed ratio is 20.50/10.22 = 2.01, still over the 2.0 swing floor. The target was not moved to rescue it — that is the manoeuvre the strategy file forbids. Note the cost honestly: 97.28 now sits 47 cents BELOW the rising SMA50 at 97.8314, so an ordinary test of that average takes the position out where 97.75 did not.

RATIO CLUSTERING IS PRESENT AND IS NOT A COINCIDENCE, so it is named rather than left to be found. Four ratios sit between 2.01 and 2.27 (DINO 2.01, XLU 2.07, XLE 2.13, EEM 2.27) against floors of 2.0, which is the signature the strategy file warns about. The defence is checkable rather than rhetorical: all four are PRE-EXISTING positions whose levels were set by the runs that opened them in August and September, not manufactured this morning — the clustering is inherited. The only levels set today are GDX's, and they land at 2.61, away from the floor. If this is attacked, the four inherited ratios are the right target, and re-opening them is a separate decision from today's. Every ratio was recomputed here from the final entry, target and downside rather than carried from the notes, and every stop was re-checked in ATRs against a freshly fetched ATR14: XLU 2.30, EEM 2.22, XLE 2.32, GDX 2.34 (ETF floor 1.8), DINO 2.00 after the amendment, SVRA 3.24 (stock floor 2.0). PFE is long-term and measured against a 23.00 bear case rather than a stop: 14.40/4.60 = 3.13 against a 2.5 floor.

EVERY CLAIMED EDGE IS SMALL, DELIBERATELY. Against the 1/(1+R:R) break-even baseline the claimed win probabilities run +2.7 to +10.9 points (XLU +9.5, DINO +2.7, XLE +8.0, EEM +5.4, GDX +8.3, SVRA +10.9). DINO's is the one that moved in synthesis: widening its stop to the floor cut the ratio from 2.10 to 2.01, which RAISES the break-even baseline from 0.323 to 0.333, so the same 0.36 win probability now claims +2.7 points rather than the +3.7 the research notes recorded — a compliant stop costs claimed edge, and that is the honest direction for it to move. None approaches the 20-point level where a thesis has to carry a large claim. These are continuations, not calls for a break. Win probability is carried through from the candidates and was not invented here; the seven closes carry none, correctly, because a market-order exit has no target-versus-stop race to handicap.

TWO CONVICTION SCORES ARE DELIBERATELY UNDER-STATED and must not be corrected upward. GDX is a 4 on four evidence kinds, because the FOMC statement and the 19-year-high 10-year yield are one fact — the Fed is hiking — read forwards and backwards off the same regime. PFE is a 4 on three kinds because the 42.00 target was NOT re-derived this morning; it is carried forward from the original thesis, so no valuation_anchor is claimed and that is said in its key_risk rather than dressed up. Conviction spread across the fourteen: one 2, seven 3s, six 4s, no 5s — and five of the seven 3s are position closes.

RANKING, since it is not a pure sort: within each conviction band, rows carrying a computable reward-to-risk are ordered by it, and the closes — which have none — are placed ahead of them because their action is due at this morning's open and is ordered by how exposed the position is (unbounded first, then nearest to its stop). Conviction 4 runs TLT, NKE, PFE 3.13, GDX 2.61, XLE 2.13, XLU 2.07; conviction 3 runs LULU, LCII, CEG, CCJ, SNX, then EEM 2.27, DINO 2.01; SVRA is the lone 2 at 3.53 and is sized as a 1% lottery ticket with one evidence kind, which its key_risk says plainly.

SEVEN CLOSES WERE MOVED WITH THEIR ORDERS INTACT, AND NONE OF THEM WAS REJECTED. TLT, NKE, LULU, LCII, CEG, CCJ and SNX are all endorsed — the structure-not-P&L rule is applied consistently across them, every arithmetic claim checked out on recomputation, and each row argues against itself honestly. They were moved because leaving them in `recommendations` publishes them badly twice over. First, the enforcement pass would demote all seven anyway and overwrite each instruction with "Demoted by validation: entry or target is missing", so the order to sell CEG would have reached the Sheet as a validation complaint. Second, and worse, `merge_report` keys a position on (symbol, direction), so a close whose direction is the opposite of the position it closes does not close anything — it OPENS A NEW ONE. Their notes now carry the order in plain words, which is where a reader looks.

THAT SECOND FAILURE HAS ALREADY HAPPENED AND IS LIVE IN THE TRACKER. state/open_positions.json carries `NKE SELL 2026-09-08 @ 38.40` and `LULU SELL 2026-09-08 @ 100.61`, both status open, both filled the day they were published, both with target None and stop None. Neither is a trade. They are the exit instructions from the 2026-09-08 report, published as recommendation rows, and they are being graded in the Performance tab today at +6.9% and -0.7% — two phantom positions in a 40-row book, one of them flattering the record by 6.9 points. `GLD SELL @ 406.77` from the same run is the pending third. The fix is code — a close is not a position and must not open one — and is out of this phase's scope, but the tracker needs it and dedupe_positions.py is the precedent for applying it backwards.

Enforcement will demote on these flags if they persist at the 2d run; that demotion is the clock, not the market.

GDX 4 to 3: two of its four evidence kinds — the 2026-09-16 FOMC statement and the hiking regime — were fully public on 2026-09-26, when this report published a GDX BUY at 91.20, three days before shorting almost the same level; synthesis already conceded those two are one fact, so stripping what was known leaves one session of price action as the new information. XLU AND PFE WERE ATTACKED AND SURVIVED UNCHANGED, said plainly rather than left to be inferred. THE RATIO FLOOR IS MEASURED TO A TARGET NOBODY PLANS TO REACH, and this is a strategy question rather than a cut. No idea was cut for it because the floor has always been applied to the full target and changing that mid-report would be a rule invented to reach a verdict, but the gap is systematic, it runs in the same direction every time, and it is the next thing check_expectancy should be asked about.

market_context.summary: One session did the work of a month, and it was a real-rates shock rather than a risk-off day. On 2026-09-28 GLD fell 3.94% and SLV 5.49% while nothing else moved more than 1.2% — SPY -0.74%, QQQ -1.07%, IWM -0.69% — with the dollar UP (UUP +0.28%), the long bond DOWN (TLT -0.88%) and crude UP (USO +1.13%). Risk-off does not sell gold; that specific combination is real rates rising, and it is the one configuration that hurts gold and everything long-duration. The driver is sourced, not inferred: the 2026-09-16 FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on a unanimous 12-0 vote, its first increase since 2023, with 16 of 18 dots seeing another this year; the 10-year closed at 5.27%, up 11bp to a 19-year high, and the 30-year at 5.55%; October 28 hike odds sit at 65-72% across sources. The proximate trigger was oil — Brent rebounded toward $106 after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting inflation fears, which lifted hike odds, which killed gold. Only three S&P sectors closed green (XLV +0.33%, XLP +0.27%, XLE +0.10%); financials were worst at -1.19% and breadth was negative. Overnight Asia was soft (Nikkei -1.11%, Topix -1.67%) against a firm Europe (Stoxx 600 +0.40%), and crude held above $105. Consequence for this book before any new idea: it was built full of long-duration equity theses — uranium build-out, datacenter power, consumer turnarounds — and a hiking cycle de-rates exactly those. Every equity and ETF price here is the 2026-09-28 close, re-quoted at 06:22 ET this morning and unchanged: that is the freshest honest price before the open, a closed market rather than stale data.
